label: que:UnmarkedLengthSpectralRigidity
title: Question
body_md:
\label{que:UnmarkedLengthSpectralRigidity}

For which $ \mathcal{ G } $ is a hyperbolic metric $ \mu $ on $ S $ determined up to isometry by its unmarked $ \mathcal{ G } $-length spectrum?
head: environment

label: que:genericIsospectrality
title: Question
body_md:
\label{que:genericIsospectrality}

If $ X $ and $ Y $ are generically unmarked simple length isospectral over $ S $, are the covers $ p $ and $ q $ isomorphic?
head: environment

label: thm:examples
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:examples}

Every closed surface $ S $ of negative Euler characteristic admits a pair of finite-degree covers which are unmarked length isospectral over $ S $ but generically not unmarked simple length isospectral over $ S $.
head: environment

label: cor:k-isospectral
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:k-isospectral}

There exist hyperbolic surfaces $ X $ and $ Y $ which are unmarked length isospectral but so that for each $ k \geq 0 $, $ X $ and $ Y $ are not unmarked $ \mathcal{ G }_{ k } $-length isospectral.
head: environment

label: thm:non-effective
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:non-effective}

The covers $ p \colon X  \xrightarrow[ #1 ]{ #2 }  S $ and $ q \colon Y  \xrightarrow[ #1 ]{ #2 }  S $ are isomorphic if and only if for every curve $ \gamma $ on $ S $, $ \gamma $ has a simple elevation along $ p $ to $ X $ if and only if it has a simple elevation along $ q $ to $ Y $.
head: environment

label: prop:lengthSpectra
title: Proposition
head: environment

label: thm:simplyGeneratedCovers
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:simplyGeneratedCovers} 

If $ p \colon X  \xrightarrow[ #1 ]{ #2 }  S $ and $ q \colon Y  \xrightarrow[ #1 ]{ #2 }  S $ are regular and simply generated, then they are either isomorphic or generically not unmarked simple length isospectral over $ S $.
head: environment
